transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-08
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Jared Cole (CTO - Nimbus), Maya Rodriguez (Head of ML - Nimbus), Samir Patel (Infra Lead - Nimbus)
Links shared: Redwood POC checklist (link: https://redwood.example.com/poc-checklist), security pack (link: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack.pdf), Nimbus sample traffic (drive: shared)

Summary:
- Scoping call to define POC success criteria and decide which deployment mode to test (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).
- Covered workload sizing, baseline benchmarks (latency/throughput), security/compliance gating, and a 4-week POC timeline option.
- Agreed next steps: pricing + sizing doc, baseline benchmark run, Nimbus to share traffic profile and network diagram, schedule infra deep-dive.

Topics: success criteria; workload profile; bench plan (p50/p95, throughput, cost); deployment tradeoffs (latency vs cost, data residency, SLAs); timeline + decision criteria.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Ethan: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intros please.
[00:10] Jared: sure, Jared Cole, CTO at Nimbus. we run the TMS and customer support agents for logistics, heavy API usage, about 18 services talk to the ai layer.
[00:18] Maya: maya here, i run ml, we're experimenting with routing and summarization, goal is to offload agents and improve RLHF tuning, um, basically, full production path.
[00:28] Samir: samir, infra. i look after cloud networking and security, lots of constraints around data residency and VPC peering.
[00:36] Priya: priya shah, solutions engineer at Redwood, i'll drive the bench plan and help size Dedicated nodes if we go that route.

[00:48] Ethan: goal for today is to align on success criteria for the POC, get a sense of traffic shape so we can recommend hosted vs dedicated vs private, and outline the benchmarks and timeline.

[01:10] Jared: high level constraints: we need sub-300ms p95 for short chat use (avg 50-100 tokens), peak concurrency around 120 concurrent requests, average daily volume ~350k requests, but burstiness is big during peak windows. also data residency EU for EU customers.

[02:05] Priya: got it. couple quick clarifying q's: is the 120 concurrency sustained or short spikes? and what's average input length distribution?

[02:18] Maya: usually spikes last 5-10 minutes, sustained baseline concurrency ~30. token distribution: 60% under 128 tokens, 30% 128-512, 10% >512. we can share anonymized logs.

[02:40] Priya: perfect. that helps. so for decision criteria here's what we typically consider: latency SLO, cost per request, data isolation/compliance, and operational control. Hosted (Redwood API) is fastest to integrate, but if you need strict VPC or on-prem rules or very predictable throughput you may look at Dedicated or Private.

[03:05] Jared: what's the rough cost delta between hosted and dedicated? like order of magnitude?

[03:12] Ethan: depends on utilization. hosted is pay-as-you-go; for your bursty profile with spikes, Hosted can be cheaper initially. Dedicated gives better unit economics once you commit to reserved capacity — you trade flexibility for predictability and lower per-token cost. Private (VPC/on-prem) adds infra and support fees. we'll send a sizing/pricing sketch.

[03:40] Samir: critically for us, any sensitive logs or customer PII must never leave our VPC; do you offer KMS integration and audit logs?

[03:50] Priya: yes, Redwood Private supports customer-owned KMS/HSM and full audit logs. Dedicated can be configured in a customer VPC in some configurations; we'll double-check network topology options. we'll include a breakdown in the security pack.

[04:10] Maya: also performance: we run reranking and embeddings for search, those are heavy on throughput. do you recommend separate clusters for embeddings vs generation?

[04:24] Priya: typically yes — embeddings and high-throughput small-token workloads often use different instance types/quantization profiles. Dedicated lets you pin model variants per route; Hosted uses smart routing but for predictable throughput Dedicated tends to be easier to optimize.

[05:02] Ethan: let's talk success criteria. what does Nimbus need to see to call the POC a win?

[05:10] Jared: three things: 1) performance: p95 latency < 250ms for <=128 tokens in production-like conditions, and p95 < 600ms for 512 tokens; 2) stability under our typical burst profile (120 concurrency spikes) with <1% error rate; 3) compliance: ability to keep EU customer data in EU region and KMS integration.

[05:40] Maya: adding quality/regression checks — we need output parity vs our current model on a 200-prompt eval set (we'll share) with acceptable delta thresholds.

[06:00] Priya: good. i'll include an eval plan: run the 200-prompt quality suite pre/post and track Rouge/BLEU/embedding-similarity and also a synthetic perf test for p50/p95.

[06:28] Jared: what benchmarks will you run during POC?

[06:32] Priya: baseline bench: cold-start single replica latency p50/p95 for 50, 128, 512 tokens; steady-state throughput with your concurrency profile; and a 1-hour spike test that mimics your 5-10 minute bursts. we'll also do token-cost estimates.

[07:01] Samir: how do you simulate caching? our platform reuses prefixes a lot, so KV cache hit rate is meaningful.

[07:12] Priya: we'll instrument KV cache scenarios — note, sometimes transcribers write "KVM" but we mean KV cache (key-value cache). we'll take sample session traces and run them to estimate effective token counts.

[07:30] Ethan: timeline suggestion: Week 0 (this week) kick-off + share assets; Week 1 baseline hosted test + baseline metrics; Week 2 Dedicated sizing and optional Dedicated pilot (if desired); Week 3 optimizations and security review; Week 4 final report and decision. so ~4 weeks.

[08:00] Jared: ok 4 weeks sounds doable. question: what turnaround for security docs and SOC/ISO stuff? we need SOC2 and ISO27001 evidence, plus penetration test summary.

[08:14] Priya: we have SOC2 and ISO certs and can share artifacts under NDA; security pack link includes cert statements and our process. for deeper info we can set up an SSO with our compliance team.

[08:40] Maya: for Dedicated, how fast to provision? if we decide Dedicated mid-POC can you spin up within a week?

[08:49] Priya: provisioning Dedicated can be 3-10 business days depending on region and capacity; we'll flag options in the sizing doc. if you need on-prem Private, that adds more lead time, typically 4-6 weeks for validation.

[09:10] Samir: network question: do you support private peering and account-level VPC peering for Dedicated?

[09:17] Ethan: yes, Dedicated supports VPC peering and Private supports full customer-controlled networking. we'll include specific topology diagrams; Samir please share your network map and we'll annotate.

[09:32] Jared: about model choices — we currently run a tuned open model plus an internal reranker. will Redwood host models or we bring our own weights?

[09:43] Priya: Redwood supports both: we can host curated open models (we'll include a catalog) and we support customer model uploads for Dedicated/Private with compatibility checks — note there are quantization and kernel constraints.

[10:05] Maya: one worry: hallucination/regression regressions after quantization. do you offer eval hooks to measure regressions automatically?

[10:15] Priya: yes, Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets/evals — we'll enable that for the POC so you can see quality metrics as we change quantization or batch settings.

[10:38] Jared: on the cost question again: if we go Dedicated with reserved commitment what kind of discount do we see?

[10:44] Ethan: discounts vary by commit; example: at 60-70% utilization on Dedicated pools you can see 25-40% lower per-token cost vs hosted; we'll put example math in the pricing doc.

[11:05] Maya: for benchmark, we want both Hosted baseline and a Dedicated pilot to compare — is it reasonable to run both?

[11:12] Priya: yep that's our recommended approach: run Hosted baseline to measure integration complexity and then spin a small Dedicated pool to compare p95 and cost under load.

[11:30] Samir: any special infra requirements for the Dedicated agents? like IP whitelisting or egress restrictions?

[11:38] Priya: we can support IP allowlists, proxying through customer egress, and private peering. we'll document specifics for your network team.

[11:55] Jared: ok, about success metrics — let's lock numbers: p95 < 250ms for <=128 tokens, error rate <1% at peak, throughput sustaining 120 concurrent spikes with warm cache and 30 req/s steady baseline.

[12:15] Ethan: sounds good. we'll include those as pass/fail criteria in the POC plan.

[12:30] Maya: how will we measure cost? per-token or per-request? we need a normalized cost for our business unit.

[12:37] Priya: we'll report both: per-request cost (based on average token consumption) and per-1M token cost; show delta between Hosted and Dedicated.

[13:00] Jared: can Redwood show observed latencies from other customers to set expectations?

[13:06] Ethan: we can share anonymized performance profiles and some benchmarks from similar customers, though not identical workloads. we'll attach a benchmark spreadsheet.

[13:30] Priya: now quick technical deep-dive highlights: for latency you care about kernel selection, KV cache warmup, and batching parameters. we can tune batch windows and continuous batching to balance latency vs throughput.

[13:50] Maya: what about model quantization? we use int8 for embeddings in production, for generation we're cautious. can Redwood run quantization trials in the POC?

[14:00] Priya: yes — we'll run quantization profiles and track quality metrics. Redwood's runtime supports quantized kernels; we will show quality deltas for each profile.

[14:20] Samir: on data residency: we require EU data to remain within EU-located GPUs. is that supported?

[14:26] Ethan: yes, we have EU regions for Hosted and can provision Dedicated in EU. Private on-prem is an option if you need total control. we'll confirm exact AZs for your needs.

[14:50] Jared: timeline recap please.

[14:53] Priya: Week 0: kick-off and asset share (this week). Week 1: Hosted baseline tests and initial quality eval. Week 2: Dedicated sizing + small Dedicated pilot (optional). Week 3: optimizations (batching, cache, quantization) and security review. Week 4: final report, cost comparison, and recommendation.

[15:20] Jared: what are blockers to start?

[15:24] Maya: we need a staging API key, a place to push sample logs, and NDA for security docs.

[15:30] Ethan: we'll send a staging API key, the POC checklist, and an NDA link.

[15:38] Priya: action items we'll put in the notes: Redwood to run baseline hosted bench (10k requests), Redwood to prepare Dedicated sizing options, Nimbus to share traffic profile and network diagram, security team exchange under NDA.

[16:00] Jared: any other concerns?

[16:05] Samir: latency SLO instrumentation — we need tracing hooks. do you provide OpenTelemetry spans?

[16:12] Priya: yes, Redwood Console exports and tracing hooks support OpenTelemetry and per-route tracing. we'll include quickstart in the docs.

[16:30] Maya: competitor question: we've evaluated OpenAI and Anthropic, do you have notes on differences?

[16:37] Ethan: short answer: Hosted Redwood offers more open-model cataloging and routing flexibility; some vendors are simpler but less configurable. we'll include a short competitive comparison.

[17:00] Jared: ok good. let's lock the immediate next steps.

[17:05] Ethan: recap: Redwood sends pricing + sizing doc (Ethan), Priya runs baseline benchmark and shares logs + dashboard (Priya), Nimbus provides traffic profile + network diagram (Maya/Samir), security docs via NDA (Ethan/Pricy? typo: priya), schedule infra deep dive week of May 18.

[17:30] Maya: thanks all. one small nit: please include a sample rollback/fallback plan if the Dedicated pilot underperforms.

[17:40] Priya: yes we'll include fallbacks: automatic routing to Hosted fallback routes and canary rollouts with progressive traffic shift.

[18:00] Jared: great, thanks everyone.

[18:10] Ethan: appreciate it. I'll send the notes and pricing tonight.

[18:20] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional misheard terms ("KVM" vs "KV cache"), timestamps approximate, speaker attribution mostly accurate but some overlap.

POC Pass/Fail (draft):
- Performance: p95 targets (<=128 tokens <250ms; 512 tokens <600ms)
- Stability: <1% error at peak bursts
- Compliance: EU data residency + KMS integration
- Quality: eval delta within agreed threshold on 200-prompt set

Attached artifacts referenced in call: POC checklist (https://redwood.example.com/poc-checklist), security pack (https://redwood.example.com/security-pack.pdf), benchmark spreadsheet (link: sent after call).

End of transcript.
